newsitem.title: USA: R.O.C. Taiwan urges rejection of conversion.
newsitem.headline: R.O.C. Taiwan urges rejection of conversion.

text.p: R.O.C. Taiwan Fund said Tuesday its board will recommend that a proposal to convert the fund to an open-end investment company be rejected by shareholders.

R.O.C., a diversified closed-end investment company registered in the United States, said a proposal to convert the fund will be submitted to shareholders for a vote at R.O.C.'s annual meeting June 3.
Adoption of the proposal would require the affirmative vote of a majority of the outstanding shares. Such a vote is required by the fund's Declaration of Trust.

The declaration provides that when the fund's shares have traded at an average discount of more than 10 percent to its net asset value over a 12-week period, a proposal to convert the fund to an open-end investment company must be presented to shareholders at the next annual meeting.
R.O.C. said this provision was triggered once before, in April 1995, and the proposal was defeated, with only 3.4 percent of the outstanding shares voting in favor.
